BEFORE THE JOINT STANDING COMNIITTEE ON INLAND FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE
IN SUPPORT OF L.D. 2236
"An Act Regarding Public Records Maintained by the Department of Inland Fisheries and
Wildlife"
Reported by Representative ROBERTS of South Berwick for the Joint Standing Committee on
Inland Fisheries and Wildlife pursuant to Resolve 2025, chapter 37, section 6.
March 23, 2026
Good afiernoon, Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts and members of the Inland Fisheries and Wildlife Committee. I am Christl Theriault, Assistant to the Commissioner and Legislative Liaison
speaking on behalf of the Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife, in support of L.D. 2236 An Act
Regarding Public Records Maintained by the Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife.
I'd like to provide a brief overview of the history of this bill. In 2025, during the First Regular Session of
the 132"" Legislature LD 101, "An Act Regarding Public Records and Fees for Requesting Public
Records from the Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife" was introduced. It was replaced with
RESOLVE 2025 CHAPTER 37 titled Resolve, to Convene a Working Group to Examine the
Classification of and Access to Public Records Maintained by Certain State Agencies. This resolve required a working group to be formed, and a report back be provided.
The Working Group had 3 meetings during the fall of 2025 during which the group discussed each of the prescribed duties within the Resolve. These discussions formed the basis for the report that I summarized
for this committee earlier in the session. The purpose of the FOAA law was at the center of the
discussions; to provide transparency and accountability within government operations, and to build public trust. Our agency collects data from our license holders, and they have an expectation that their personal information will be protected and used as an avenue to communicate fish and wildlife matters, not to be shared for commercial purposes.
The Working Group played a key role in shaping LD 2236, which responds to the department's primary legal and operational concerns while aligning FOAA principles and proven models used by other
agencies. The members reviewed and refined the draft legislative language to amend Title l2, Part 13.
The legislation addresses MDIFW's authority related to licenses, permits, and registrations, it defines
personally identifiable information (PII), records and data. It also describes what records or data would be
held confidential within public records requests associated with these records.
With the bill being drafted so late in the session we didn't see the draft bill prior to printing. The formatting is significantly different than what was provided by the Working Group and there are some omissions, additions, and inconsistencies we found that we feel should be corrected if this committee is
supportive of passing the bill. We took the time to provide the suggested edits as an attachment to this
testimony.
Please follow along LD 2236 bill language while I explain the intent of each section. When I get to a
section that has a suggested amendment, I will refer to the page and line number. You're welcome to have
l

the proposed amendment document next to the bill to refer to, that has all the bill language and anything to be changed is highlighted in yellow.
Sec 1. Repeals current law that allows an applicant for a hunting or fishing license to indicate that the applicant's e-mail address is confidential and that requires that information be held confidential by the Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife. This has been problematic for the agency to implement so
rather than allowing someone to indicate that they want their email address to be kept confidential we implemented a policy keeping all emails confidential. The new bill proposes to clearly allow the agency
to keep all emails confidential.
Sec 2. It creates a new section of law related to records held by the department and databases the
department contributes to which hold the department's licenses, permits, registrations and applications. The bill also defines "data," "commercial record," "noncommercial record" and "personally identifiable information" within a noncommercial record and within a commercial record.
IFW's proposed changes to Sec. 2.

0 Page 1, Line ll. & 12. Modifies the definition of data to include that the data may be contained
on paper or electronic medium and not just in an electronic medium. It adds that data "may be"
contained in a database. This allows for data that might be contained in a paper booklet submitted by a trapper, captive wildlife holder or taxidermist, as just a few examples.
I Page 1, Lines 18, 28, 29 & 30. Within the definition of personally identifiable information, we
are requesting to strike: (1) a person's name, (10) information contained in any free text data field
and (11) any other infonnation contained in a data field that may be used to identify a person. The
Revisor's office included names and the free text data fields as confidential to be consistent with another section of the bill related to crash reporting. The protection of this information within the crash reporting section of law serves a very specific purpose, to prevent commercialization of that
information. Many law firms and other companies seek to exploit crash report data to generate
business.
I Page 1, Line 34. Add "data or" to any PII included in any record. v Page 2, Lines 9., 13.-15. Simplify the language by replacing whole or partial database records
with the defined term "data" .
There is more personally identifiable information held confidential for a noncommercial record than for a commercial record which is intentional. The Working Group felt that commercial license holders such as guides, taxidennists and those commercially fishing should be willing to have some of their contact information released. The bill provides exceptions for holding personally identifiable information confidential, including exceptions for law enforcement purposes in accordance with Title 16, section 805A, fish and wildlife management purposes, other state and federal government entities and the person who
is the subject of the record or that person's agent.
The bill provides that data contained in a records database, whether individual or multiple records,
maintained, administered or contributed to by the department that is considered confidential may not be
publicly disseminated.
The bill provides that the department may charge reasonable fees at the expense of the person making the request, may publicly disseminate nonpersonally identifiable information and may provide copies of
individual records and data to individuals, businesses and other entities. The cost of fumishing a copy of
the record is not subject to the limitations of Title l, section 408~A (FOAA law).
2

Sec 3. & 4. Sections 3 & 4 of the bill create ATV and snowmobile accident reporting system exemptions that mirror
the Department of Public Safety's exemption for motor vehicle crash report data which is held in the
Maine Crash Reporting Online Search and Ordering Service. These provisions allow any nonpersonally
identifiable ATV and snowmobile accident report data to be released to the public, and the cost to process
these data requests and release the records is not subject to the limitations within Title 1, section 408-A
(FOAA law). These sections also create definitions for "data," "nonpersonally identifiable accident report
data" and "personally identifiable accident report data."

The bill also provides that ATV and snowmobile accident reports or statements contained within have
specific uses for law enforcement purposes and the agency can disseminate individual records or multiple
records in accordance with this law. ATV and snowmobile registration numbers may be released only
under an affidavit restricting the use and misuse of registration numbers, and failure to comply with
reporting obligations is a Class E crime.

The Working Group ultimately gave unanimous support to, and the Department agreed to remain focused
on changes to MDIFW's authority by helping craft and review the proposed bill language you have before

you which in short does the following:

1. Strengthens privacy protections around PII in hunting, fishing, trapping and recreational vehicle licensing systems and recreational vehicle accident reports.
2. Clarifies what data is confidential vs. releasable, for both recreational (noncommercial) type
license records and for commercial type license records.
W 3. Expands ease of access to non-identifiable statistical data by allowing Infor1\/[E clear authority
to charge a requestor from the public, reasonable fees for more expeditious access to MDIF
records held within a database, while preventing the public release or misuse of PII.

For these reasons, the Department strongly supports this bill.
